chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Mis'mam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who was in the state of Ihram in the Sanctuary (al-Haram) and threw a spear at game outside the Sanctuary, killing it, he said: 'Upon him is the compensation (diyah), because the injury came to the game from the side of the Sanctuary.'
And whoever has some of the game with him, let him leave it when he enters Ihram and let him remove it from his ownership. Narrated.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْجَزَاء: Compensation or expiation (diyah) for killing game
key_terms.الْحَرَم: The Sanctuary (specifically Mecca/Medina), a sacred area with specific rules

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing game from inside the Haram boundary while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *al-afah* (the source of the harm) in determining liability for game killed by a pilgrim, establishing that the sanctity of the location where the act originates dictates the ruling. It further prescribes a practical precaution (*ihtiyat*) of divesting ownership of game before entering Ihram to prevent accidental violation. This ruling is central to the jurisprudence of *Damm* (compensation) and illustrates the Shia emphasis on precise attribution of cause in ritual law.
